hook: Seven people, a 40-foot boat, 69 miles out in 10-foot seas.
narration: Seven people on a forty-foot fishing boat, sixty nine miles out, in seas near ten feet.
It was a Sunday off Cape May, New Jersey, with a small craft advisory and wind gusting to thirty knots.
As conditions got worse, the crew set off their emergency beacon.
That beacon sends a distress signal and its position by satellite, so rescuers know exactly where to fly.
A Jayhawk helicopter and a Hercules plane launched from Air Station Elizabeth City, North Carolina.
One at a time, the helicopter crew hoisted them out of the rough water.
They had life jackets, a registered beacon, and a radio, which they used to call for help.
outcome: All seven people were hoisted and taken to Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City.

extra_sources.excerpt: CAPE MAY, N.J. — The Coast Guard rescued seven people from a sport fishing boat beset by weather 69 miles southeast of Cape May Sunday.
A small craft advisory for the area indicated 4-to-6-foot seas with winds gusting up to 30 knots.

Watchstanders at Coast Guard Sector Delaware Bay received the initial report from Coast Guard Sector Virginia at 1:19 p.m., stating that a 40-foot sport fishing boat with seven people aboard had been beset by weather with seas reaching approximately 10 feet.

The crew of the vessel activated their Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) when conditions continued to deteriorate. Coast Guard crews aboard an MH-60 Jayhawk and an HC-130 Hercules aircraft from Air Station Elizabeth City, North Carolina, and a 47-foot Motor Life Boat from Station Indian River were launched to assist.
All seven people were hoisted and taken to Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City where local EMS was standing by to assist.
Fortunately, they had life jackets, a registered EPIRB and a radio, which they used to call for help.
